title: Thermodynamics, Rate Equations and Kp
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Chemistry: Thermodynamics and Rate Equations Worksheets
standard_text: Entropy, Gibbs free-energy change and feasibility, rate equations, orders of reaction and rate constants, the Arrhenius equation, and equilibrium constant Kp for homogeneous systems.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level chemistry worksheets on thermodynamics and kinetics: entropy, ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, rate equations, orders, rate constants and their units, the Arrhenius equation and Kp. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; feasible when ΔG ≤ 0.
key_sub: Change ΔS from J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ into kJ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
body_html:
How to think about it

A reaction is feasible when ΔG = ΔH − TΔS ≤ 0. The temperature at which it becomes feasible is T = ΔH/ΔS (with matching units). ΔS = ΣS(products) − ΣS(reactants).

A rate equation has the form rate = k[A]m[B]n; the orders come from experiments, not the equation. k = Ae−Ea/RT. For gases, Kp uses partial pressures: p = mole fraction × total pressure.

Example

ΔH = +178 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔS = +161 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Minimum T?

T = 178000 ÷ 161

Answer: 1110 K

Example

Doubling [A] quadruples the rate. Order in A?

2² = 4

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

  • Mixing kJ and J in ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.
  • Taking orders from the balanced equation.
  • Using °C in the Arrhenius equation.

faq.q: What does a negative ΔG mean?
faq.a: The reaction is feasible (it can happen without continuous energy input), though it may still be slow.

faq.q: How do you find the order of a reaction?
faq.a: Change one concentration at a time: if the rate stays the same the order is 0, doubles → 1, quadruples → 2.

items.q: For a reaction ΔH = −180 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = −90 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔG at 500 K.
items.e: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = −180 − 500 × (−0.0900) = −135 kJ mol⁻¹. Change ΔS into kJ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ first.
